question: Does one closed structural-feature vocabulary, with every value routed to one current constructor or profile, one listed Core reopening condition, or one explicit boundary, deterministically classify every frozen case without using protocol-family names as rules?

derivation.breaks: At least one selected value routes to an explicit_boundary destination.
derivation.bends: No selected value routes to an explicit_boundary destination and at least one selected value routes to a reopening_condition destination.
derivation.fits: Every selected value routes to a constructor destination.

destinations.summary: Exactly one Prover and one Verifier, with PublicEnvironment as the non-party public source.
Public parameters, statements, and initial public bindings supplied by PublicEnvironment.
Verifier-private invocation inputs, values, queries, answers, and local randomness.
Prover-private inputs, random tapes, observations, and local state remain in ProverView or Plan.
Statement material is fixed in scope before every challenge that may depend on it.
A typed verifier challenge is an occurrence with an explicit source and dependency boundary.
One challenge occurrence may be shared by explicit reference without duplicating its source.
Classical typed messages carry public, prover-private, or verifier-private dependencies under the Core visibility rules.
Verification predicates and declared reductions are explicit Core nodes.
Accept, Reject, and Abort use first-active terminal semantics with a required fallback.
Initial or prover-published immutable Oracles support FullCanonical, PublicBinding, and Logical access with public or verifier-only queries.
Oracle declarations and effects are optional when the interaction has no oracle access.
A typed semantic module owns a finite acceptance-relevant transition that is not a plain Boolean check.
Finite sequential, interleaved, and concretely elaborated composition flattens to one admitted Core.
Plan owns private material, one-shot randomness, persistent local state, and decision recipes.
A finite folding or accumulation step may hand an accepted result to a named continuation under Plan ownership.
Imported Boolean verification is a Core Check; richer finite transitions use ModuleEffect; predicate proofs belong to Relations.
Verifier-fresh challenges, including private-coin challenges, remain a Fresh construction rather than a hash execution.

destinations.section: 3 Canonical transcript frames and 9 Challenge rules
destinations.summary: A transcript-derived challenge uses the canonical framed transcript and declared sampling interpretation.
A selected duplex sibling construction uses one continuous state and explicit squeeze occurrences.
Grinding is a prior challenge plus private search, a public nonce, and an explicit check.

destinations.section: 11 Logical Oracle access and commitment compilation
destinations.summary: A logical Oracle is distinct from a commitment and may be related by a separately checked commitment construction.
A finite closed verifier-derived word program elaborates completely to ordinary source queries and unchanged flat Core.
A required statement component is fixed only after the first challenge.
A symbolic recurrence cannot be lowered to a feasible and semantics-preserving finite Core.
A required oracle or preprocessing lifecycle cannot inhabit the immutable Section 7 Oracle model.
Verifier-private information is necessary for relation grounding but cannot be disclosed under the current boundary.
An acceptance-relevant effect cannot state its exact transition, visibility, influence, replay, or bounds.
Independent noncommunicating provers and physical multiparty transcript semantics are outside v0.
Distributed verifier knowledge and multiple verifier-private views are outside v0.

destinations.section: 4.1 Parties and 14 Composition and family boundaries
destinations.summary: A protocol lifecycle requiring more than the Prover and Verifier roles is not one current Core invocation.
Data-dependent, prover-chosen, verifier-chosen, or scheduler-nondeterministic topology is outside finite Core composition.
Unbounded interaction or a required nonterminating execution is outside v0.
A challenge imported from another execution lacks a current same-session occurrence and transcript-owner construction.
A prover-selected value cannot be relabelled as a verifier Challenge occurrence.
Answer-adaptive query-plan topology is Unsupported; only an explicit finite Core may express the corresponding dependence.
An open stream, PCD network, or cross-execution protocol state is not flattened as one finite Core.
Concurrency and inter-session transcript ownership are not supplied by finite same-session composition.
The current typed classical value and message carrier has no quantum state, channel, measurement, or no-cloning semantics.
The cited source omits the transform or acceptance semantics needed to classify the complete construction; the result remains CannotAnswer.
